recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The current core source already reflects the final FHIR-35974 decision after the FHIR-34467 implementation and subsequent rename; no additional core edit is needed unless the work group later changes the retained other mode.
issue_request: FHIR-35974 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 SearchParameter. It asked to trim the old xPathUsage/renamed usageMode code set: the description identifies nearby and distance as unsupported generic modes and questions other, while the final resolution keeps other and says to remove location/distance. Because the historical code system had nearby and distance but no location code, location appears to be a resolution-wording slip for nearby.
initial_application: No local source commit explicitly mentions FHIR-35974. The Jira comment says it is the same as FHIR-34467 and cites PR 1964. Commit 1a0b67ee41d08eb9ca386b8e6312a456846cba43 (FHIR-34467) removed nearby and distance from source/searchparameter/codesystem-search-xpath-usage.xml while leaving normal, phonetic, and other.
additional_context: SearchParameter is active in source/fhir.ini, and the old SearchParameter.xpathUsage element maps to SearchParameter.processingMode. Later rename commits b75dfd27696fceaf6c23be15323b69cd482ff3e6 and 6372dc2225d155526d2d170be97344f1bd35daa9 changed search-xpath-usage to search-processingmode and updated the StructureDefinition binding. FHIR-I minutes for 2022-04-25 record the FHIR-35974 vote to remove the unsupported spatial codes and keep other.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current source/searchparameter/codesystem-search-processingmode.xml contains only normal, phonetic, and other; source/searchparameter/structuredefinition-SearchParameter.xml advertises processingMode as normal | phonetic | other with a required binding to ValueSet/search-processingmode; and a targeted source search found no remaining nearby/distance processing-mode concepts.
